title: The internet feels super lonely right now. Here's why

mock_data.title: The internet feels super lonely right now. Here's why
mock_data.passage:
Almost 80 years ago, sociologists identified a new personality type that is particularly sensitive to loneliness. It's even more relevant today, says Annalee Newitz

Right now, I'm glued to my phone. Like most people in the US, I get my news from various apps – social posts, podcasts, newsletters – and when things are blowing up (literally) I can't look away. People in Minneapolis are posting video updates from protests; experts are publishing essays about international law and the US attack on Venezuela. I have to consume them all! The weirdest part, though, is that the more I watch and read what other people are saying, the lonelier I feel.

This is hardly a new or unique experience. Sociologists have been talking about it for nearly 80 years. In 1950, scholars David Riesman, Nathan Glazer and Reuel Denney published a book called The Lonely Crowd, in which they argued that the rise of consumerism and mass media had led to a new kind of personality type that is deeply sensitive to loneliness. They called this personality "other-directed", and their descriptions feel startlingly prescient in our era of social media and AI chatbots.

Other-directed people are constantly attuned to what everyone around them is doing, using the preferences of their peer groups to decide what to buy, wear and think. Because their values come from peers, rather than elders or ancestors, they tend to be present-oriented and unconcerned with history. Riesman and his colleagues warned that other-directed people are obsessed with conforming, anxious to be "part of a crowd" and "having fun". What other-directed people fear more than anything is being alone.

All of these personality traits are immediately recognisable to people dealing with social media, with its peer pressure, parasocial relationships with influencers and – especially these days – surveillance capabilities. We are always watching each other and being watched. And because we fear being alone, companies produce apps designed to fool us into thinking we aren't. That's one of the insidious things about AI chatbots, some of which are designed to act like friends.

There's a paradox in every other-directed person's heart. As much as we may want to conform, to be part of the group chat, we also want to feel like we are unique. Riesman and his colleagues explained that consumerism itself assuages this other-directed anxiety by offering "false personalisation". You experience this when you find yourself choosing between six virtually identical polo shirts at the store. Picking one might make you feel that there's a special brand out there just for you, but, fundamentally, all those shirts are the same. You wind up wearing a polo shirt just like everybody else.

This kind of false personalisation shows up all the time in the algorithms that shape our experiences online. TikTok and other apps have a "for you" feed full of videos that feel tailor-made for your specific tastes. And yet it is shaped by an algorithm that you don't control, whose purpose is largely to keep your eyeballs glued to the same app that everyone else is glued to. It is "for you" in the service of conformity.

As other-directed people, we are invited to express ourselves mainly by participating in peer groups or by "joining the conversation", as so many ads suggest. We turn ourselves into internet content, adding our words and videos to the morass of others online. Be yourself by showing that you are doing what everybody else is doing!

And yet we still feel lonely. Partly that's because in-person friendships and communities are fundamentally different from online ones. But something else is going on here, and I think it has to do with the personality shifts chronicled in The Lonely Crowd. When we cobble ourselves together out of what we think other people want, we hide from something crucial: our own truly personal, messy, eccentric, non-conformist desires. We can't connect with other people in a genuine way if we don't know ourselves.

Riesman and his co-authors suggested two solutions to this other-directed problem. First, we need to take back our leisure hours from the hyper-consumerist sphere of media. All that effort we put into paying attention to our peers is too much like work, they argued, and we need more free play. Which brings me to their second suggestion, which is that people – and especially kids – should test out new identities and experiences. Figure out what you enjoy when nobody is telling you what "fun" is supposed to be. Do something you have never done before. Wear something dramatic or silly. Strike up a conversation with a neighbour you have never met. Surprise yourself. And see how it feels to just... experiment.

You won't figure out who you are from a "for you" feed or a chatbot. So get off your phone, do something unexpected and be yourself for a while.

What I'm reading
Notes From a Regicide, by Isaac Fellman, a fantastical tale of rebellion and family drama.

What I'm watching
Heated Rivalry, because I know how to have fun.

What I'm working on
Researching Sogdiana, my favourite ancient diaspora culture.

Annalee Newitz is a science journalist and author. Their latest book is Automatic Noodle. They are the co-host of the Hugo-winning podcast Our Opinions Are Correct. You can follow them @annaleen and their website is techsploitation.com

mock_data.translation:
Deyarli 80 yil oldin, sotsiologlar yolg'izlikka ayniqsa ta'sirchan bo'lgan yangi guruhdagi (shaxsiyat tipini) shaxslarni aniqladilar. Bu bugungi kunda yanada muhimroq, deydi Annali Nyuvis (Annalee Newitz).

Hozir men telefonimga mixlanib qolganman. AQShdagi ko'pchilik odamlar singari, men ham yangiliklarni turli ilovalardan – ijtimoiy postlar, podkastlar, xabarnomalardan – olaman va vaziyat (tom ma'noda) qizib ketganda men ko'zimni olib qocholmayman. Minneapolisdagi odamlar namoyishlardan video yangilanishlarni joylashtirmoqda; mutaxassislar xalqaro huquq va AQShning Venesuelaga hujumi haqida maqolalar e'lon qilmoqda. Men ularning barchasini ko'rishim kerak! Ammo eng g'alati tomoni shundaki, boshqa odamlarning nima deyayotganini qancha ko'p ko'rsam va o'qisam, o'zimni shunchalik yolg'iz his qilaman.

Bu mutlaqo yangi yoki noyob tajriba emas. Sotsiologlar bu haqda qariyb 80 yildan beri gapirib kelishadi. 1950 yilda olimlar Devid Risman, Natan Gleyzer va Ruel Denni "Yolg'iz olomon" (The Lonely Crowd) degan kitob nashr etishdi, unda ular iste'molchilik va ommaviy axborot vositalarining kuchayishi yolg'izlikka chuqur ta'sirchan bo'lgan yangi shaxsiyat tipining paydo bo'lishiga olib kelganligini ta'kidlashgan. Ular bu shaxsiyatni "boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan (other-directed)" deb atashgan va ularning ta'riflari bizning ijtimoiy tarmoqlar va AI chatbotlari davrimizda hayratlanarli darajada to'g'ri (oldindan ko'ra oluvchi) tuyuladi.

Boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan odamlar nima sotib olishni, nima kiyishni va nima deyishni hal qilishda doimo atrofdagi tengdosh guruhlarining tanlovlariga ergashishadi, ya'ni atrofidagilar nima qilayotganidan doim xabardor bo'lishadi (moslashishadi). Ularning qadriyatlari oqsoqollar yoki ajdodlardan emas, balki tengdoshlaridan kelib chiqqani uchun ular ko'proq bugungi kun bilan yashaydigan bo'lishga va tarix bilan qiziqmaslikka moyildirlar. Risman va uning hamkasblari boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan odamlar qoidalarga bo'ysunishga (moslashishga) mukkasidan ketganligi, "olomonning bir qismi" bo'lishga va "ko'ngil xushlik qilishga" doim bezovta(intiq) bo'lishlari haqida ogohlantirganlar. Boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan odamlar eng ko'p qo'rqadigan narsa - bu yolg'iz qolishdir.

Bu shaxsiy xususiyatlarning barchasi darhol ijtimoiy tarmoqlardagi odamlar orasida ko'zga tashlanadi: uning tengdoshlar bosimi, ta'sir o'tkazuvchilar (influencers) bilan bo'lgan bir tomonlama munosabatlar va – ayniqsa shu kunlarda – kuzatuv (surveillance) imkoniyatlari tufayli. Biz har doim bir-birimizni kuzatib turamiz va o'z navbatida o'zimiz ham kuzatuv ostidamiz. Va biz yolg'iz qolishdan qo'rqqanimiz uchun, kompaniyalar bizni unday emasligimizga ishontiruvchi ilovalar ishlab chiqaradi. Ba'zilari do'stlar kabi harakat qilish uchun yaratilgan AI chatbotlarining hiyla-nayrangli (bildirmay zarar yetkazadigan) tomonlaridan biri ham shundadir.

Har bir boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan insonning qalbida bir paradoks mavjud. Biz guruh chatining bir qismi bo'lishni, unga moslashishni qanchalik xohlasak, shu bilan birga noyob ekanligimizni his qilishni ham xohlaymiz. Risman va uning hamkasblari shuni tushuntirishdiki, iste'molchilikning o'zi "soxta moslashtirishni (shaxsiylashtirishni)" taklif qilish orqali ushbu boshqalarga yo'naltirilganlik tashvishini pasaytiradi(yumshatadi). Siz do'konda bir xil bo'lgan oltita polo futbolkasidan birini tanlayotganingizda ushbu holatga duch kelasiz. Ulardan birini tanlash sizni aynan o'sha erda o'zingiz uchun maxsus brend borligini his qilishingizga olib kelishi mumkin, ammo, asosiy jihati shundaki, bu futbolkalarning hammasi bir xil. Oxir-oqibat siz xuddi hammaga o'xshab bir polo futbolkasini kiyib yurasiz.

Bunday soxta shaxsiylashtirish bizning onlayn tajribamizni shakllantiruvchi algoritmlarda har doim namoyon bo'ladi. TikTok va boshqa ilovalarda sizning ma'lum didingizga ko'ra maxsus tayyorlangandek tuyuladigan "siz uchun" ("for you") tasmali videolari bor. Va u shunday bir algoritm asosida shakllantirilganki, siz uni nazorat qila olmaysiz; uning maqsadi asosan hamma mixlanib qolgan xuddi shu ilovaga sizning ko'zingizni ham mixlab qo'yishdir. Bu bir xillikka(bo'ysunishga) xizmat qiladigan "siz uchun(for you)" dir.

Boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan odamlar sifatida biz ko'pincha tengdosh guruhlarimizda qatnashish yoki ko'p reklamalar taklif qilganidek, "suhbatga qo'shilish" orqali o'zimizni namoyon qilishga taklif qilinamiz. Biz o'zimizni onlayn platformalardagi boshqa odamlarning so'zlari va videolari botqog'iga qo'shilgan holda internet kontentiga aylantirib qo'ymoqdamiz. Hamma nima qilayotgan bo'lsa, siz ham shuni qilayotganingizni ko'rsatish orqali o'zingiz bo'ling!

Va shunga qaramay, biz hali ham o'zimizni yolg'iz his qilamiz. Qisman buning sababi amaldagi shaxsiy do'stliklar o'rnatish va jamoalar onlayn muloqotlardan tubdan farq qiladi. Ammo bu erda boshqa bir narsa ham bor va bu "Yolg'iz olomon" da qayd etilgan shaxsiyat o'zgarishlari bilan bog'liq deb o'ylayman. Qachonki biz boshqalar nima xohlaydi deb o'ylab o'zimizni yig'ib tayyorlasak, biz o'ta muhim bo'lgan bir narsadan yashiringan bo'lamiz: bu bizning haqiqiy shaxsiy, tartibsiz, g'ayrioddiy, qoidalarga bo'ysunmaydigan istaklarimizdir. Agar o'zimizni bilmasak, boshqa odamlar bilan haqiqiy aloqa o'rnata olmaymiz.

Risman va uning hammualliflari bu boshqalarga yo'naltirilgan muammoga ikkita yechim taklif qilishdi. Birinchidan, biz dam olish soatlarimizni ommaviy axborot vositalarining o'ta iste'molchi muhitidan tortib olishimiz kerak. Ular tengdoshlarimizga e'tibor berish uchun sarflaydigan barcha harakatlarimiz huddi ishlashga o'xshab qoldi va bizga ko'proq erkin o'yinlar (bo'sh vaqt) kerakligini ta'kidlashgan. Bu meni ularning ikkinchi taklifiga olib keladi: odamlar - ayniqsa bolalar - yangi xususiyatlarni va tajribalarni sinab ko'rishlari kerak. Sizga hech kim "qiziqarli(ko'ngilxushlik)" nima ekanligini aytmayotgan bir paytda, nima sizga zavq berishini bilib oling. Ilgari hech qachon qilmagan ishingizni qiling. Kulgili yoki e'tiborni tortadigan narsa kiying. Siz ilgari ko'rmagan qo'shningiz bilan suhbat boshlang. O'zingizni hayratda qoldiring. Shunchaki... biror narsani tajriba qilib ko'rish qanday ekanligini his qiling.

Siz "siz uchun" tasmasi orqali yoki chatbotlardan o'zingiz kimligingizni anglay olmaysiz. Shunday ekan, telefoningizni qo'ying, kutilmagan biror narsa qiling va biroz muddat o'zingiz kabi bo'ling!

Men nima o'qiyapman
Ishoq Fellmanning ("Notes From a Regicide") isyon va oilaviy drama haqidagi ajoyib hikoyasi.

Men nima tomosha qilyapman
("Heated Rivalry"), chunki men qanday zavqlanishni bilaman.

Men nima ustida ishlayapman
O'zim yoqtirgan eng sevimli qadimiy diaspora madaniyatim – Sug'diyona(Sogdiana)ni o'rganyapman.

Annali Nyuvis – bu yozuvchi va fan jurnalisti. Ularning so'nggi kitobi ("Automatic Noodle"). Ular Gyugo (Hugo) mukofotiga sazovar bo'lgan "Fikrlarimiz to'g'ri (Our Opinions Are Correct)" podkastining hammuallifi hisoblanishadi. Ularni @annaleen va ularning techsploitation.com veb-saytida kuzatib borishingiz mumkin.
